history.period: Date of construction unknown (local legend predates the present structure)
history.summary: The temple at Jhalmala is about 60 km from Bhilai. Per local lore, a fisherman found an idol of the goddess caught in his net in the neighbouring water body but did not notice it and let it pass ignored; a villager later dreamt he was instructed to recover the idol and install it in a hut near the village, and Bhikam Chand Tiwari later built a temple in its place. Navratri is the major occasion here, with long-distance barefoot pilgrimages to the temple. Founding date and builders UNVERIFIED. CSV town 'Bhilai' corrected: actual town is Jhalmala (Balod district, carved out of Durg district in 2012; older sources still list Durg). Coordinates are approximate (Jhalmala village locality), precision unverified.

name: Ganga Maiya Temple, Bhilai
town_description: Jhalmala is a small agricultural village in Balod district, Chhattisgarh (part of Durg district before Balod was carved out in 2012), on the Durg-Dalli-Rajhara road about 60 km from Bhilai. Paddy is the main crop and the local economy is agrarian. The Ganga Maiya temple makes the village a local pilgrimage destination, especially during Navratri when devotees arrive in large numbers.

travel.airport: Swami Vivekananda Airport, Raipur (~90 km, verify)
travel.road: On the Durg-Dalli-Rajhara road, about 60 km from Bhilai town

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Navratri for the festive atmosphere
